body_markdown:
As of this writing, the most expensive road-going[Ferrari 550 Maranello](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/the-550-maranello-laid-the-groundwork-for-ferraris-next-30-years/) ever sold at a public auction is[a 527-mile 1998 model](https://www.broadarrowauctions.com/vehicles/ql26_r0072/1998-ferrari-550-maranello) that Broad Arrow Auctions sold for $648,500 in August 2026. The record might not stand for very long: Joopiter and Curated are selling a 1997 550 Maranello that was bought new by former NBA player Michael Jordan and that has been hidden for over 20 years.


Assigned chassis number 108712, this Rosso Barchetta-finished 550 was delivered new to Jordan on May 29, 1997, by Foreign Cars Italia in Greensboro, North Carolina. Joopiter notes that the factory warranty card included in the sale shows the five-time NBA MVP’s signature and Durham, North Carolina, address. The car features chrome-finished Speedline wheels, a tan interior, and a modified driver’s seat with extended rails and thinner padding to allow Jordan, who stands 6’6″, to fit behind the wheel.


Jordan presumably owned many cars while he played for the Chicago Bulls, yet he drove the 550 Maranello on a regular basis. He was notably photographed in the driver’s seat with a cigar in his hand after winning his fifth NBA Championship on June 13, 1997. The car wore Illinois registration number “MJ 5,” so it was easy to recognize, and it became so closely associated with Jordan that it reportedly inspired Tinker Hatfield to design a shoe called Air Jordan XIV with unmistakably Ferrari-like logos on both sides.


The 550 had covered about 6400 miles when Jordan sold it through an Illinois dealership on December 4, 2002. Where it ended up was a mystery until earlier this year, when Curated co-founder John Temerian found it in California after a decade-long search. It was kept by its second owner in a private collection, and it had never been publicly offered for sale since Jordan traded it in.

Luckily, the past 24 years have been kind to the 550. It’s a manual model with under 19,000 miles, so it would be desirable even if it wasn’t celebrity-owned. The second owner kept service records, including the ones detailing maintenance performed during Jordan’s ownership that list the registration number as “MJ 5.” It hasn’t been significantly modified; it has even retained its Ferrari-branded cassette player, so it looks pretty much like it did when it was owned by one of the greatest basketball players of all time.


Michael Jordan’s 1997 Ferrari 550 Maranello will be displayed publicly at CART Department in New York City from September 15 to 20, and interested buyers will be able to see it in person by appointment after that. Bidding will open on September 15 and close on September 30. Joopiter and Curated expect to sell this piece of basketball history for between $700,000 and $1.3 million.


The 550 stands out as the first car sold by Joopiter, an e-commerce platform founded by Pharrell Williams. The site normally sells sports memorabilia, fashion items, and other collectibles. Joopiter plans to sell more cars through its partnership with Curated, so starting with Michael Jordan’s Ferrari is a smart move. This sale could make it a credible player in the growing car-auction world.
